newsitem.title: UK: UK Telecoms group wants new rules on chatlines.
newsitem.headline: UK Telecoms group wants new rules on chatlines.

text.p: A UK industry-funded watchdog group called on Wednesday for new rules over telephone chatlines, including refunds for unauthorised calls and messages warning users of amounts spent.

The Independent Committee for the Supervision of Standards of Telephone Information Services (ICSTIS) said in a statement that the guidelines were for "virtual" chatlines, in which callers exchange recorded messages.
ICSTIS said there should also be a requirement to obtain confirmation from callers that they wish to continue the calls.

"If bills are disputed, consumers must be confident that valid and reasonable claims will be met by the industry, which is why we are recommending a new code of practice provision to this effect," ICSTIS director Sarah Harrison said in a statement.
ICSTIS called for responses to its proposals, in a paper entitled "Virtual Chat and Live Premium Rate Services - A Statement," by October 10.
The group said around 15 million calls are made annually in the virtual chat sector, estimated to be worth 30 million stg, while the premium rate industry is valued at some 160 million stg.
Operators of premium rate services are bound by contracts with network operators to abide by the provisions of the ICSTIS code of practice.
Network operators include British Telecommunications Plc, Cable and Wireless Plc, Orange Plc and Vodafone Value Added Services.
